questions.q: The number of 6-letter words, with or without meaning, that can be formed using the letters of the word MATHS such that any letter that appears in the word must appear at least twice, is _______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
(i) Single letter is used, then no. of words $=5$
(ii) Two distinct letters are used, then no. of words
${ }^5 \mathrm{C}_2 \times\left(\frac{6!}{2!4!} \times 2+\frac{6!}{3!3!}\right)=10(30+20)=500$
(iii) Three distinct letters are used, then no. of words
${ }^5 \mathrm{C}_3 \times \frac{6!}{2!2!2!}=900$

Total no. of words $=1405$

questions.q: Some couples participated in a mixed doubles badminton tournament. If the number of matches played, so that no couple played in a match, is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>840</mn></math>, then the total numbers of persons, who participated in the tournament, is ________.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

Some couples participated in a mixed doubles badminton tournament. If the number of matches played, so that no couple played in a match, is 840,

Now Let total number of persons be 2n, so number of couples will be n

Now number of matches played, so that no couple played in a match is given by,

⇒C2n·C2n-2·2=840

{as if we choose couple as A,B and other couple as C,D and taking other two couple as x,y & w,z, so the possible combination of the match  where no couple played in a match will be, A,x→C,w & C,x→A,w , hence there are two possible combination after choosing }

⇒nn-1n-2n-3=5·6·7·8

So, n=8

Hence, the number of persons will be, 2n=16

questions.q: Let <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math> be the set of all passwords which are six to eight characters long, where each character is either an alphabet from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="{" close="}"><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>D</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>E</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> or a number from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="{" close="}"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> with the repetition of characters allowed. If the number of passwords in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>S</mi></math> whose at least one character is a number from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="{" close="}"><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></mfenced></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>5</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given total available characters is 10 and total digits are 5,

So, for 6-digit password, the number of ways =106-56

For 7-digit password, the number of ways =107-57

For 8-digit password, the number of ways =108-58

∴  Total ways =106+107+108-56+57+58

=2656+2757+2858-56-57-58

=5626+5·27+25·28-1-5-25=7073·56

Now on comparing with α×56 we get α=7073

questions.q: The largest natural number <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>n</mi></math> such that <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mi>n</mi></math> divides <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>66</mn><mo>!</mo></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi><mi>_</mi></math>
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We know that,

Maximum value of n for pn where p is prime divides the number a! is given by,

 ap+ap2+ap3+ap4+...

Since, 3 is a prime number, so we have

=663+6632+6633+6634+...

=22+7+2+0

=31

So, maximum value of n is 31.

questions.q: For $\mathrm{n} \geq 2$, let $S_n$ denote the set of all subsets of $\{1,2 \ldots . . ., n\}$ with no two consecutive numbers. For example $\{1,3,5\} \in \mathrm{S}_6$, but $\{1,2,4\} \notin \mathrm{S}_6$. Then $n\left(\mathrm{~S}_5\right)$ is equal to ________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{A}=\{1,2,3,4,5 \ldots . . . \mathrm{n}\}$
No. of subsets having $r$ elements such that no two are consecutive is $={ }^{n-r+1} C_r$
for $\mathrm{n}=5$, no. of ways $={ }^{6 \cdot \mathrm{r}} \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{r}}$
Subsets having no element $=1$
Subsets having exactly 1 element $={ }^5 \mathrm{C}_1=5$
Subsets having exactly 2 element $={ }^4 \mathrm{C}_2=6$
Subsets having exactly 3 element $={ }^3 \mathrm{C}_3=1$
$\Rightarrow 5+6+1+1=13$

questions.q: If <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mmultiscripts><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn><none/><mprescripts/><none/><mn>1</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>·</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>P</mi><mn>2</mn><none/><mprescripts/><none/><mn>2</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>·</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>P</mi><mn>3</mn><none/><mprescripts/><none/><mn>3</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>+</mo><mo>…</mo><mo>+</mo><mn>15</mn><mo>·</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>P</mi><mn>15</mn><none/><mprescripts/><none/><mn>15</mn></mmultiscripts><mo>=</mo><mmultiscripts><mi>P</mi><mi>r</mi><none/><mprescripts/><none/><mi>q</mi></mmultiscripts><mo>-</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>≤</mo><mi>s</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>1</mn></math>, then <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mmultiscripts><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow><none></none><mprescripts></mprescripts><none></none><mrow><mi>q</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>s</mi></mrow></mmultiscripts></math> is equal to
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have,

P11+2·P22+3·P33+…+15·P1515=Prq-s

where, 0≤s≤1

Now,

1P1+2·2P2+3⋅3P3+…+15·15P15

=1!+2·2!+3·3!+……+15·15!

=(2!-1!)+(3!-2!)+(4!-3!)+……+(16!-15!)

∵n·n!=n+1-1n!=n+1!-n!

=16!−1!=Prq−s

⇒q=r=16 & s=1

So,

Cr-sq+s=C1517=17×162=136

questions.q: In an examination, <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math> students have been allotted their seats as per their roll numbers. The number of ways, in which none of the students sits on the allotted seat, is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
5 boys with allotted roll numbers and seat numbers are seated in such a way that no one sits on the allotted seats. The number of ways of such seating arrangement is equal to the derangement of 5 boys i.e.,

=5!1-11!+12!-13!+14!-15!

=5!-5!+60-20+5-1

=44

questions.q: The number of 3-digit numbers, formed using the digits $2,3,4,5$ and 7 , when the repetition of digits is not allowed, and which are not divisible by 3 , is equal to__________
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
total number of three digit numbers not divisible by 3 will be formed by using the digits
$\begin{aligned}
& (4,5,7) \\
& (3,4,7) \\
& (2,5,7) \\
& (2,4,7) \\
& (2,4,5) \\
& (2,3,5) \\
& \text { number of ways }=6 \times 3 !=36
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Consonants are L, T, T, R

Vowels are E, E,

Total number of words (without meaning) from letters of word 'LETTER'=6!2!2!=180

Total number of words (with or without meaning) from letters of word 'LETTER' if vowels are together =5!2!=60

∴ Required =180-60=120

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:

7 Red appleRA

8 oranges O

Now, for offering 5 fruits to be selected 

Possible selections :- (2O, 1RA, 2WA) or 2O,2RA,1WA,  or 3O,1RA,1WA

Required number of ways

=C28C17C25+C28C27C15+C38C17C15

questions.q: The sum of all <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math>-digit numbers less than or equal to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>500</mn><mo>,</mo></math> that are formed without using the digit <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn></math> and they all are multiple of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>11</mn><mo>,</mo></math> is ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
209,220,231,........,495 series in A.P.

Clearly, a=209, d=220-209=11 and l=495

Where a is the first term, d is the common difference and l is the last term.

⇒l=a+n-1d=495

where n is the number of terms

⇒l=209+n-111=495

⇒n-111=286

⇒n-1=26

⇒n=27

Sum=2722×209+26×11=27209+143=27×352=9504

Numbers containing 1 at unit place =231, 341, 451

Numbers containing 1 at 10th place =319, 418

Hence, required sum of all 3-digit numbers less than or equal to 500=9501-231+341+451+319+418=7744

questions.q: All the letters of the word <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>G</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>W</mi><mi>E</mi><mi>N</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>Y</mi></math> are written in all possible ways with or without meaning and these words are written as in a dictionary. The serial number of the word <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>G</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>W</mi><mi>E</mi><mi>N</mi><mi>T</mi><mi>Y</mi></math> IS
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
We have to find the rank of word GTWENTY.

Words starting from E=6!2!=7202=360

Words starting with GE=5!2=60

Words starting with GN=5!2=60

Words starting with GTE=4!=24

Words starting with GTN=4!=24

Words starting with GTT=4!=24

Then the next word will be GTWENTY and its rank will be 360+60+60+24+24+24+1=553

questions.q: The total number of three-digit numbers, with one digit repeated exactly two times, is ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
For three digit number we have following cases,

Case I: When digit zero is repeated

Number of numbers =C19=9

Case II: When digit zero is present but not repeated

Number of numbers =C19·2!=18

Case III: When digit zero is not present

Number of numbers =9·8·3!2!=216

Total number of numbers =243

questions.q: The total number of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn></math>-digit numbers, whose greatest common divisor with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>36</mn></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn></math>, is ______.
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Prime factorisation of 36=2×2×3×3

So, for number having G.C.D with 36 to be 2, the number should be odd multiple of 2 and does not have factor 3 and 9

⇒Odd multiple of 2 are

102,106,110,114…….998  225 numbers

⇒No. of multiples of 3 are

102,114,126…….990 75 numbers

Which also include multiple of 9

Hence, Required =225-75=150

questions.q: The number of ways, 5 boys and 4 girls can sit in a row so that either all the boys sit together or no two boys sit together, is $\qquad$ -
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
A : number of ways that all boys sit together $=5!\times 5!$
B : number of ways if no 2 boys
sit together $=4!\times 5$ !
$\mathrm{A} \cap \mathrm{B}=\phi$
Required no. of ways $=5!\times 5!+4!\times 5!=17280$
